item.title: Report: 26 US sites across Middle East damaged in Iranian attacks
item.description:
Report: 26 US sites across Middle East damaged in Iranian attacks

Over 115 strikes claimed by Iran or groups aligned with Tehran have damaged 26 military bases and other infrastructure belonging to the US across the Middle East, The Associated Press reported. 

The analysis, using satellite imagery, indicated that Iranian attacks on US sites in the region have mostly targeted early-warning systems, aircraft and buildings, resulting in billions of dollars’ worth of damage to US equipment.

item.title: Watch: Mosque torched in northern Israel, graffiti sprayed on walls
item.description:
Watch: Mosque torched in northern Israel, graffiti sprayed on walls

A mosque was set on fire, and Hebrew graffiti calling for revenge was sprayed on its walls in the Palestinian village of Ed-Dahi in northern Israel on Thursday.

Palestinian citizens described the incidents as acts of "terror", which they also said came after weeks of escalating incitement against their community following record voter turnout and electoral gains in last month’s elections.

item.description:
Pentagon official says US war on Iran cost $48.3B

A Pentagon official told lawmakers that the US war on Iran has cost an estimated $48.3 billion.

"That number includes munitions, equipment replacement costs, and operational cost," Arthur Miller said. 

However, the figure does not include the price of repairing US military installations in the region damaged since February.

item.title: US Senate blocks Iran war powers resolution
item.description: The US Senate on Thursday blocked a war powers resolution directing President Donald Trump to withdraw American forces from hostilities with Iran, Anadolu reports. The upper chamber voted 48-51 against adopting the measure, H.Con.Res. 93. Three Republican senators — Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul — broke with most of their party to support the resolution. Sen. John Fetterman was the only Democrat to vote against the measure, while Sen. Chris Murphy did not vote. In September, the House of Representatives approved the measure, which was sponsored by Democratic Rep. Seth Moulton, by a vote of 220-204. item.title: Egypt, Libya sign cooperation agreements after talks in Cairo
item.description: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi and Libyan Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibeh discussed ways to strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, energy and reconstruction on Thursday, according to a statement from the Egyptian presidency. The talks took place during Dbeibeh’s visit to Cairo, where Sisi welcomed him, and the two sides witnessed the signing of several agreements and memoranda of understanding. Sisi highlighted the need to boost trade and investment ties, and cooperation in the energy and reconstruction sectors in a way that serves the mutual interests of both countries. The Egyptian president also reaffirmed Cairo’s commitment to supporting security and stability in Libya and preserving its unity and territorial integrity. item.title: Israeli airstrikes hit eastern Lebanon, target homes, buildings in south
item.description: Israeli warplanes carried out five airstrikes on a mountainous area in eastern Lebanon on Thursday, while additional airstrikes, drone attacks and artillery shelling targeted several towns in the south, according to Lebanese state media. Lebanon’s official National News Agency (NNA) said five strikes hit the Al-Shaara area in the Anti-Lebanon mountain range, near the outskirts of Janta village in the eastern Baalbek district. The explosions were heard in the city of Baalbek, the agency said. No casualties were reported. The Israeli military said its air force had carried out an intelligence-guided strike in the Janta area of Lebanon’s eastern Bekaa Valley. German rights group seeks arrest of former Mossad chief for Lebanon attacks
item.description: A leading German rights group filed a criminal complaint Thursday against former Mossad chief David Barnea, demanding his arrest upon entry into Germany for alleged war crimes he committed in Lebanon, Anadolu reports. The Berlin-based European Center for Constitutional and Human Rights, known as ECCHR, filed the complaint with the Federal Public Prosecutor’s Office.
